featured_reviews.name: Raj_Tayade
featured_reviews.review_text: Church of St Andrew and St Columba (or Scots' Kirk) is a church with two separate buildings located in Kala Ghoda (St Andrew) and Fort (St Columba) in Mumbai, India. It was Bombay's first Scottish church and was built in 1819 after the arrival of the city's first Presbyterian minister, James Clow, who was appointed chaplain for the East India Company in 1815 The two Scottish churches were merged in 1938 The architectural style of St Andrew is Greek revival and the facade is said to have been inspired by St Martin-in-the-Fields in London Both St Andrew and St Columba are only open on Sundays for service, and on other days the latter is used for the church's homeless street children project.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visiting St. Thomas Cathedral in Fort, Mumbai felt less like ticking off a heritage checklist and more like stepping into a quieter, more reflective version of the city—one that still breathes calmly despite the chaos outside. Tucked amidst the rush of office-goers, traffic signals, and colonial-era buildings, the cathedral stands with a grace that doesn’t demand attention, yet effortlessly commands respect.

What struck me first was the sense of calm the moment I entered the premises. The noise of Fort seemed to fade instantly, replaced by a soft stillness that felt almost therapeutic. It’s rare to find such a space in South Mumbai where time seems to slow down, inviting you to pause, observe, and simply be present. The cathedral isn’t just visually beautiful; it has an emotional weight to it—one that gently nudges you towards introspection.

The architecture is understated yet powerful. There’s no excessive ornamentation, but every element feels purposeful. The high ceilings, elegant arches, and stained-glass windows allow natural light to pour in, creating an atmosphere that feels warm and welcoming rather than intimidating. As sunlight filters through the glass, the interiors take on a soft glow, making it an ideal place to sit quietly, even if only for a few minutes.

What I appreciated most was how alive the space feels, despite its age. This isn’t a museum frozen in time; it’s a living landmark that continues to serve as a place of worship, community, and history. Reading the plaques and memorials, you’re reminded of the countless lives and stories that have passed through these walls—stories of colonial Bombay, changing times, and enduring faith.

St. Thomas Cathedral is not just for those interested in religion or history. It’s for anyone seeking a moment of calm, a connection to Mumbai’s layered past, or simply a peaceful corner to gather their thoughts. Every visit leaves you a little lighter, a little calmer, and with a renewed appreciation for the quieter, soulful side of the city.

featured_reviews.name: Foodieextreme Foodieextreme
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited July 15, 2025 – Day 12 in India

After visiting the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya museum, our guide brought us to St. Thomas Cathedral—a beautiful and deeply historic church nestled in the heart of Mumbai. Built in the early 1700s, it’s the city’s oldest Anglican church and feels like a peaceful sanctuary surrounded by history.

What took me by surprise were the many graves laid directly into the floor. I made sure my husband and our daughters, ages five and seven, were careful not to step on any. My girls noticed a small white grave and were curious if it belonged to a child. When we read the inscription, we saw that it was for a 54-year-old woman, the wife of an officer. That moment sparked quiet reflection and curiosity in all of us.

Inside, we saw the seat where Mother Teresa had once sat, which was marked with a small plaque. Nearby were two elegant seats once used by King George V and Queen Mary during their visit in 1911. My husband and daughters loved the experience of sitting in those very seats, imagining what it must have been like over a century ago.

What I personally loved most was the peace I felt in the church. Before this trip, many people had asked me to pray for them, knowing this journey was meaningful to me on a spiritual level. In the stillness of the cathedral, I took time to sit quietly and pray for each of them. It was a heartfelt and emotional experience.

We left with calm hearts and lasting memories. I truly loved this visit.

featured_reviews.name: ANIMESH SHUKLA
featured_reviews.review_text:
St. Thomas’ Cathedral is one of Mumbai’s most historic and beautiful churches, offering a serene escape in the bustling Fort area. Built in 1718, it is the oldest Anglican church in Mumbai and an essential part of the city's colonial heritage. The church, now part of the Church of North India (C.N.I.), is not just a place of worship but also a significant historical monument.

Historical Importance: As Mumbai’s first Anglican church, St. Thomas’ Cathedral played a crucial role in the city's colonial past. It was built during British rule and remains a testament to the city's rich history.
Stunning Architecture: The church features classic Neo-Gothic and colonial architectural styles, with elegant arches, stained glass windows, and intricate carvings that transport you back in time.
Peaceful Ambience: Despite being in the heart of the bustling Fort area, the church’s interiors are calm and soothing, making it a perfect place for reflection and prayer.
Well-Preserved Memorials: The walls of the cathedral are adorned with memorial plaques dedicated to British soldiers and officers, offering a glimpse into Mumbai’s past.
UNESCO Recognition: The cathedral is a part of the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensemble of Mumbai, which has been recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Visiting Experience
Best Time to Visit: Morning hours are ideal for a quiet and spiritual experience. The church is open to visitors on most days.

Surroundings: Located near Horniman Circle, it is close to landmarks like Flora Fountain, Bombay High Court, Rajabai Clock Tower, and the Asiatic Library.

Mass Timings: If you wish to attend a service, check their schedule beforehand, as Sunday Mass is particularly special.

Photography: While photography is allowed in most areas, it’s best to be respectful as it is an active place of worship.

St. Thomas’ Cathedral is a must-visit for history buffs, architecture lovers, and anyone looking for a moment of peace in Mumbai’s fast-paced environment. Whether you admire its heritage, attend a service, or simply enjoy its quiet beauty, this cathedral is truly a hidden treasure in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Google 4 U
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bowen Memorial Methodist Church in Colaba, Mumbai, is a charming and historically significant church that stands as a testament to Mumbai’s colonial past. Located in a quieter part of bustling Colaba, it offers a peaceful and reflective atmosphere that provides a welcome escape from the city’s hectic pace.

The church’s architecture is a blend of Gothic Revival with some colonial influences, making it a visually striking structure. The stained glass windows and wooden interiors add to its charm, making it an ideal spot for those who appreciate historical buildings with spiritual significance.

Visitors often mention the sense of tranquility they experience upon entering, and the serene ambiance makes it an ideal place for both personal reflection and prayer. The church isn’t typically crowded, allowing for moments of peace in a busy city.

Given its location in Colaba, it’s also conveniently near other iconic landmarks like the Gateway of India, making it a great stop for those exploring the area. Whether you're a history enthusiast or someone seeking a peaceful retreat, Bowen Memorial Church offers a delightful blend of spirituality, architecture, and heritage.

Bowen Memorial Methodist Church holds historical significance, as its cornerstone was laid by **Bishop J. M. Thoburn**, the first Methodist Episcopal Bishop of India, on **2nd February 1889**. This pivotal moment marks the church’s deep connection to the early spread of Methodism in India. Bishop Thoburn was a key figure in establishing the Methodist presence in the country, and his involvement adds a layer of historical and religious importance to the church. Visitors who are aware of this heritage often feel a deeper connection to the church’s legacy and its role in the spiritual history of the region.

name: Wesley Church ( C.N.I )
description:
Wesley Church, earlier known as the Wesleyan Methodist Military and Naval Church, was the first British Methodist Church to be built in India. The foundation stone was laid on March 14, 1890, and it was opened for public worship in March 1895. Rev. George W. Clutterbuck was the first Presbyter of the church. Along with the church, a high school and medical mission was also started in 1887.
The church houses a pipe organ, which is over 100 years old and was built in the early 1900s by Conacher and Company, Huddersfield, U.K. It's a tracker action organ with two manuals and pedals, three divisions, 16 ranks, and three couplers.
All are welcome to come and worship at the church.
Worship Service is held every Sunday at 10 am.

featured_reviews.name: Muhammed Wajeeh
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Afghan Church, officially the Church of St. John the Evangelist, is a historic Anglican church located in Colaba, Mumbai, dedicated in 1858. Built to honor soldiers who died in the First Anglo-Afghan War (1839–1842), it is a Grade-I heritage structure known for its stunning Gothic Revival architecture, featuring a 198-foot steeple, ornate stained glass, and a poignant "war memorial" design.
Key Details About The Afghan Church:
Location: Duxbury Lane, Navy Nagar, Colaba, Mumbai.
Purpose: Served as a memorial for the East India Company troops who died in the Afghan campaigns (first Afghan war).
Architecture: Designed by architect Henry Conybeare, the structure features buff-colored basalt and Porbunder stone, high vaulted ceilings, and early English Gothic style.
Restoration: The World Monuments Fund (WMF), Church of North India (CNI), and Indian Navy completed a major three-year restoration to restore its roof, windows, and structural elements.
Key Features:
Stained Glass: Beautiful windows created by William Wailes from England, installed between the 1850s and 1890s.
Rifle Pews: Features unique wooden pews with slots designed for soldiers to hold their rifles.
Memorials: Contains extensive records of soldiers who died in the wars.
Management: It is an active Anglican place of worship.
The church is located in a military area (Navy Nagar) and serves as a quiet landmark reflecting Mumbai's colonial and military history.

featured_reviews.name: Divyansh Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Afghan Church in Mumbai is a stunning architectural gem located on the shores of the Arabian Sea. This historic church, also known as St. John the Evangelist Church, boasts a unique blend of neo-Gothic and Moorish styles, reflecting the city's colonial past.

A Serene Escape

Visiting the church on weekdays is highly recommended, as it's usually less crowded, allowing for a peaceful and introspective experience. You can sit, relax, and immerse yourself in the calm atmosphere, making it an ideal spot for self-reflection. The filtered sunlight streaming through the stained-glass windows creates a serene ambiance, perfect for unwinding.

History and Significance

Built between 1847 and 1858, the Afghan Church commemorates the soldiers who lost their lives during the First Afghan War. Its historical significance and architectural beauty make it a must-visit destination in Mumbai ¹.

Tips for Your Visit

- Best time to visit: Early mornings or late afternoons for optimal lighting
- Dress modestly, showing respect for the church's religious significance
- Photography is allowed, but be mindful of worshippers
- Explore the surrounding gardens for a peaceful retreat

Getting There

The church is located in Navy Nagar, Colaba, and is easily accessible by public transportation. You can take a local train from Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CST) or a taxi/auto-rickshaw from there.

Overall, the Afghan Church is a beautiful and historic spot that offers a serene escape from Mumbai's hustle and bustle. Visit during the week to experience its tranquility and soak in its stunning architecture.
